fills.researcher_notes: ONE QUESTION PER COMPANY, decided once and applied identically to both built-pipe rows in this brief (P3273, P5788; not flagged on P6712, which has no physical pipe yet and no Operator flag). Answer: АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия» / Intergas Central Asia JSC. Sourcing: (1) intergas.kz's own 'About company' page states ICA received 'статус Национального оператора по магистральному газопроводу' by Government of RK Resolution (July 2018) and explicitly lists its regional divisions -- УМГ «Актау», «Актобе», «Шымкент», «Кызылорда» -- as each operating 'МГ «Бейнеу-Бозой-Шымкент»' by name (all four regions the BBS route crosses). (2) rus.baq.kz, an independent Kazakh news outlet, corroborates the same July-2018 national-operator designation on the same date (a wire-independent, editorially separate report of the same government act -- not a rewrite of an ICA press release). (3) intergas.kz/kz/news/4/653 (Kazakh-language) is ICA's own announcement that its Central Dispatch Control specifically for МГ «Бейнеу-Бозой-Шымкент» began operating, i.e. a BBS-specific operational claim, not just a general remit. Value is unchanged from the current sheet ('Intergas Central Asia'); this fill only supplies the missing ref. Note the distinct corporate roles found while researching: a bsgp.kz article on the Turkestan compressor-station launch calls КазТрансГаз the 'национальный оператор' commissioning the asset in a ceremonial/corporate sense, while ICA's General Director attended as the O&M subsidiary's head -- i.e. KazTransGas/QazaqGaz is the OWNER/holding-level actor, ICA is the day-to-day pipeline operator. That distinction is exactly what the sheet's separate Owner vs Operator cells already encode, so it does not conflict with this fill.

validity.researcher_notes: Beineu-Shymkent Gas Pipeline LLP's own 'About company' page (bsgp.kz) states the JV 'was established on the basis of equal share participation of two countries', with KazTransGas JSC (Kazakhstan) and Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline (China, with CNODC/a CNPC subsidiary as ultimate shareholder) each contributing 50% of the $1bn charter capital, and that this LLP is the entity that 'accepted the functions of the Project company' -- i.e. it is the owner/project vehicle for the pipeline P3273 describes (Phase I, built 2011-2015). This is a physically and corporately distinct joint venture from the QazaqGaz-UCC Holding (Qatar) partnership that is building Phase II (P5788) and its planned capacity uprating (P6712, 'III (Capacity expansion)') -- confirmed via QazaqGaz/UCC Holding press material (epcintel.com, qazinform.com, PRNewswire Feb-2024) describing UCC Holding and Power International Holding as QazaqGaz's partner for 'the second line of the Beineu-Bozoy-Shymkent pipeline' specifically, with no Chinese-side involvement mentioned. The gem.wiki page's 'union' merges these two unrelated JVs (Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline Co Ltd + China Reform Holdings on one side, UCC Holding + Power International Holding on the other) across all three rows because it describes the whole multi-phase system on one page -- this is the multi-segment wiki-union artifact the protocol describes, not a sheet defect. The sheet's existing per-row differentiation (P3273 carries the China-side names, P5788/P6712 carry the Qatar-side names) is already correct and should be left alone.

validity.researcher_notes: In 2015, PetroChina (CNPC) divested 50% of its stake in Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline Co Ltd to CNIC Corporation Limited, a Hong Kong-based subsidiary of China Reform Holdings Corp, for roughly $2.3-2.4bn, while retaining the other 50% itself -- i.e. Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline Co Ltd's parent is now SPLIT 50/50 between PetroChina/CNPC and China Reform Holdings Corp, not a single parent. This matches gem.wiki's inclusion of 'China Reform Holdings Corp' as a Parent candidate for this system, but the wiki drops PetroChina's retained 50%, so simply adopting the wiki value would be half-right. Two trade-press sources describe the same 2015 transaction (nsenergybusiness.com and pipeline-journal.net) but both plausibly trace to the same original wire story (neither cites the other's primary filing), so tier is medium and independence is marked false pending a primary corporate-registry or PetroChina-disclosure source.
